heading: INT. CLOCK REPAIR SHOP - AFTER HOURS

units.text: INT. CLOCK REPAIR SHOP - AFTER HOURS
A narrow shop crowded with ticking.
Wall clocks, mantel clocks, cuckoo clocks, a grandfather clock with its door ajar.
A green banker's lamp lights the workbench.
Rain on the window glass.
ELSPETH FAIRWEATHER (60s, silver braid, brass loupe pushed up on her forehead, ink-stained apron) sits at the bench with a pocket watch open under the lamp.
She works the tweezers with a surgeon's calm.
A cassette recorder rests at her elbow, the red light on.
She lays the tweezers down.
She presses her thumbnail into the watch case.
A hidden catch springs open.
Inside the lid, something is engraved.
She squints.
She lowers the loupe over one eye.
Wednesday. The pocket watch from the widow. The engraving inside the lid reads "M.H. to A.H., never late."
units.name: ELSPETH

units.text: She lifts her head.
The shop ticks on.
She counts the strokes of one nearby clock and frowns.
That one is slow. Four seconds, and always four seconds.
units.name: ELSPETH

units.text: She rises.
She crosses to a mantel clock and opens its back.
She examines the works, closes it, steps away.
A second clock is slow.
A third.
She stands in the center of the shop, listening.
A hundred tickings, each a heartbeat out of time with its neighbor.
On the bench, the recorder clicks.
She turns back and finds the tape has run out.
She presses rewind.
It whines.
She presses play.
Wednesday. The pocket watch from the widow.
units.name: ELSPETH

units.text: Her own voice from five minutes ago.
She stands very still.
After her recorded sentence, another voice enters, low and dry, a man's.
Don't turn around.
units.name: ELSPETH

units.text: She turns around.
The shop is empty.
The grandfather clock's door stands open.
Behind it, in the dark case where the pendulum should swing, nothing hangs but shadow.
She does not scream.
She reaches back, finds the recorder without looking, and holds it in both hands.
I never said that.
units.name: ELSPETH

units.text: The pendulum, which had not been moving, begins to swing.
I should never have opened that watch.
units.name: ELSPETH

units.text: She lifts the pocket watch from the bench.
She turns it to the lamp.
The engraving, "never late," has changed.
Someone has etched a date beneath it, today's, and a time.
Eight forty.
She checks the wall clock.
It is eight thirty-eight.
Elspeth sets down the recorder.
She takes up the tweezers again, calmly, as if to repair something.
Behind her, the tickings synchronize, one by one, until all hundred clocks beat together.
